title: I'm building a Forza Horizon–style open-world racer set in Russia: Moscow, St. Petersburg and Krasnaya Polyana on one map (solo dev + a team of AI agents)
author: pytodai
selftext:
Hey! I'm a programmer, new to gamedev, and I'm building a Horizon-style open-world racing game set in Russia, just for me and my friends to drive together online.

The twist: my "team" is AI agents. One model leads and writes most of the code, a second one is the chief reviewer and tries to break every design and every commit, and a third checks renders and in-game images. There's even a small "Blender team" of agents (modeler, materials, tech artist, QA) that builds assets from scripts.

What exists after 2 days (very early, greybox):

* Custom simcade car physics in pure C#: raycast suspension, a slip-based tire model, drivetrain with an LSD, 100 Hz with substeps, 110+ physics tests
* A 2.8 km handling loop / proving ground (skidpad, slalom, jumps, bumps, dirt)
* Online for friends (Unity Netcode, each player simulates their own car). Two game instances already drive together.
* Unity 6.3 + URP, Mac and Windows

Next up: the first real car (Nissan GT-R R35), then the map: central Moscow, central Petersburg and the mountain roads of Krasnaya Polyana, compressed into one map like FH does.

Happy to answer questions about the AI-agent workflow or the physics!

comments.author: allangod
comments.body: If you plan to monetise it the furst issue you'll come across is us8ng the real cars without permission.

replies.author: pytodai
replies.body: Totally fair point. It's not for sale: it's a private hobby project for me and a few friends, no monetization. If it ever went public, real cars would get fictional names and designs.

comments.author: Plourdy
comments.body: How are you planning to make the maps? Can AI intelligently layout and place props and such? Utilize terrain tools, all that good stuff?

replies.author: pytodai
replies.body: Great question! The plan is to build terrain from real elevation data (Copernicus DEM) and roads from OpenStreetMap, so the layout is grounded in the real places, compressed FH-style. Buildings in Moscow/Petersburg would be generated from OSM footprints with style-matched facades, landmarks done separately, and AI helps with props and placement rules. The agents are good at the pipeline/tooling side; the "does this look like Russia" judgment stays with me.
